labels.label: prop:mesure_admissible

hypotheses.note: instance: M = E_0 (Causal.E0, OQ-34/OQ-35). E0.mesure_admissible is SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible fed E0.singularFlatAxioms, E0.isCausal and E0.modelMeasures; the first instance with sing_0 nonempty

mesure_admissible uses E0.isCausal only (as the abstract theorem does); E_0 is strongly causal anyway (E0.stronglyCausal), and the open form ModelRowsE0.e0_stronglyCausalOpen supplies the paper's U_p in paper_measures_local

hypotheses.paper: hypothesis (i): lambda_3 + lambda_1 (past) and lambda_3 (future) restricted to a relatively compact causally convex U_p (l.1734-1743)
hypotheses.note: paper_measures_local: every neighbourhood of every point contains such a U_p, with (volume + lam1).restrict U_p admissible in the past on U_p and volume.restrict U_p in the future. ModelMeasures itself is fed with U = E_0 and the finite measures muMinus, muPlus (Measure.toFinite), as timelikeLine_modelMeasures does

hypotheses.paper: lambda_3, 'the Lebesgue measure of R^3' (l.1737); lambda_1, 'the Lebesgue measure of sing(E_0) = R' (l.1739)
hypotheses.note: volume on E_0 = R x C; lam1 = image of Lebesgue measure under tau -> (tau, 0). Harmless: every finite measure with the same null sets is admissible (admissible*_of_equiv). See questions

hypotheses.paper: hypothesis (ii): monotonicity of K^- and K^+ (l.1745-1746)

findings: ETT.tex:1737-1741, at E_0, holds as printed. lambda_3 satisfies properties 1, 3, 4 in the future (Causal.E0.lam3_future). lambda_3 + lambda_1 satisfies them in the past (Causal.E0.lam3_add_lam1_past). 'The singular term is exactly what property 3 in the past requires along a BTZ line' is sharp: lambda_3 alone satisfies 1 and 4 in the past and fails 3 at two axis points (Causal.E0.lam3_past_profile).

ETT.tex:1742-1743, 'Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p'. For property 4 this is correct as stated: for A in U_p, J^-_U(A) \ K^-_U(A) = (J^-(A) \ K^-(A)) cap U_p. For property 3 it needs more than property 3 of the model. With J^-_U(x) = J^-(x) cap U_p, one needs mu((J^-(q) \ J^-(p)) cap U_p) > 0, and mu(J^-(q) \ J^-(p)) > 0 does not give it. It does hold for lambda_3 and lambda_3 + lambda_1, because J^-(q) \ J^-(p) meets every neighbourhood of q: in a non-empty open set off the axis, in an axis segment ]p,q] on it. Lean: Causal.E0.pos_past_inter, pos_future_inter, used by admissiblePastOn_restrict_of and admissibleFutureOn_restrict_of. By hand, not formalized: on Minkowski 3-space a finite measure equivalent to lambda_3 restricted to {t < -1} is admissible in the past, since J^-(q) \ J^-(p) meets every slice {t = s}, s << 0, in a set of positive area. It vanishes on every U_p inside {t > -1}. So the bare inference fails, and only the paper's particular measures make the step true. Suggested wording: '... and, J^-(q) \ J^-(p) meeting every neighbourhood of q in a non-empty open set or, at a BTZ point, in a segment of the singular line, Lemma restriction_convexe turns ...'.

The planner's [r] route was checked step by step and is correct. (1) r -> (u + r, r e^{i theta}), r >= 0, is chronological (Causal.E0.lt_ray: ClosedLt reads r1 < r2 and 0 < (r2 - r1)^2). The frontier of any <<-past or <<-future set meets each such curve at most once, for open and non-open sets alike (frontier_ray_subsingleton_of_past, _of_future). The shear (tau, z) -> (tau - |z|, z) preserves lambda_3 (Causal.MeasuresE0.measurePreserving_shear, a skew product over the identity of C). Polar coordinates close each u-slice (volume_eq_zero_of_ray_subsingleton). (2) The 'at most one axis point' claim in property 4 in the past holds: such a point x has tau(x) = max over A of f, and the maximum is attained (isGreatest_fcoord_of_mem_axis_inter, axis_inter_Jminus_diff_Kminus_subsingleton). The bound is sharp: at a BTZ point p the set is {p} (axis_inter_Jminus_diff_Kminus_axis). (3) Property 3 holds as planned. (4) The planner's Gaussian weighting is replaced by Measure.toFinite (same null sets, no integral to compute).
questions: Which measures are lambda_3 ('the Lebesgue measure of R^3', l.1737) and lambda_1 ('the Lebesgue measure of sing(E_0) = R', l.1739) on E_0? The paper's coordinates (tau, r, theta), read Cartesian, would give d tau dr d theta = (1/r) d lambda_3. Reading taken: lambda_3 is Lebesgue measure on R x C, the coordinates (tau, z) of Causal.E0; lambda_1 is the image of Lebesgue measure on R under tau -> (tau, 0). Harmless: properties 1-4 see a measure only through its null sets, its positivity on open sets and axis segments, and (for U_p) its finiteness on compacts. Every finite measure in the class of lambda_3 (resp. lambda_3 + lambda_1) is admissible in the future (resp. past) (admissibleFuture_of_equiv, admissiblePast_of_equiv).

labels.label: rem:singular_flat_spacetime_therefore

hypotheses.note: instance: M = E_0 (E0.singularFlatAxioms; E0.singularFlatSpacetime also holds)
the library has no differentiable structure (as in SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_hypotheses)

the library's list (SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_hypotheses): metrizable, locally compact, tarentin, causally arc-connected, strongly causal, J^±(p) != {p}, and the pair of admissible measures, now discharged at E_0 by E0.modelMeasures

findings: ETT.tex:1508-1510, at E_0, with strong causality (DEC-18), holds: E_0 satisfies every hypothesis of theo:geroch the library records, including a measure admissible in the future and one admissible in the past (Causal.E0.geroch_hypotheses). This is the first instance with a BTZ line; the only earlier one was the timelike line (sing = empty). The consumers of ModelMeasures are also non-vacuous at E_0: theo:geroch_sing (i)=>(ii) and (i)=>(iii) give a Cauchy time function and a Cauchy surface (Causal.E0.geroch_sing_i_imp_ii, geroch_sing_i_imp_iii; E0.globallyHyperbolic).

labels.label: rem:mesure_unilaterale

hypotheses.note: instance: M = E_0 (E0.isCausal); SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_unilaterale fed E0.singularFlatAxioms

hypotheses.paper: p < q two BTZ points of one singular line (l.1717)
hypotheses.note: the axis of E_0 is not empty (E0.singE0_zero_nonempty); the abstract theorem asks only sing_0 nonempty

findings: ETT.tex:1713-1723, at E_0, holds. The ledger note 'No witness with a BTZ point' is stale: the remark is non-vacuous at E_0 (Causal.E0.mesure_unilaterale_sharp). Each one-sided notion is inhabited (muMinus in the past, muPlus in the future), and no measure is in both. 'Property 4 is the obstruction' (l.1715-1716) is concrete there. The segment ]0,1] of the axis lies in J^+(0) \ K^+(0), and lambda_3 + lambda_1 charges it (lam3_add_lam1_not_null_future); this is the paper's computation of l.1719-1722. Meanwhile lambda_3 + lambda_1 satisfies properties 1 and 3 in the future (lam3_add_lam1_future_profile). Dually, muPlus fails property 3 in the past (muPlus_not_pos_past).

kb_proposals: Lebesgue-null frontiers at E_0 without charts: vertical lines tau -> (tau, z) are null in E_0, so ConeNull's vertical sections do not apply. Use the chronological curves r -> (u + r, r e^{i theta}) (Causal.E0.lt_ray), then the shear and polar coordinates: Causal.MeasuresE0.volume_eq_zero_of_shear_ray_subsingleton, Causal.E0.volume_frontier_of_past and _of_future (any <<-past or <<-future set, open or not).

To get a finite measure with the null sets of an s-finite one, use mu.toFinite (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.WithDensityFinite). The lemmas toFinite_absolutelyContinuous, absolutelyContinuous_toFinite and toFinite_apply_eq_zero_iff live in namespace MeasureTheory, not MeasureTheory.Measure. No Gaussian density is needed. A finite measure on R x C is Regular by instance (Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure).

Property 3 of defi:mesure_dieckmann does not pass to a causally convex open V by lem:restriction_convexe alone. Prove its local form, 0 < mu((J^-(q) \ J^-(p)) cap W) for every open W containing q (Causal.E0.pos_past_inter, pos_future_inter). Then Causal.E0.admissiblePastOn_restrict_of and admissibleFutureOn_restrict_of restrict any measure with the right null sets.

ModelMeasures with a BTZ point is Causal.E0.modelMeasures (U = E_0). The paper's local form, lambda_3 + lambda_1 and lambda_3 restricted to a relatively compact causally convex U_p, is Causal.E0.paper_measures_local. mesure_admissible, geroch_hypotheses, mesure_unilaterale and geroch_sing_i_imp_ii/iii are instantiated at E_0 under the same names in Causal.E0.
